2609.03553.title: GPS-Bench: A Governance Policy Benchmark for Automating Policy Analysis
2609.03553.paper_summary: Policy analysis requires more than predicting whether a proposal will pass: it requires identifying who will be affected, how those actors respond, and what follows. LLM-based policy simulations model these processes at scale, but their validity is hard to establish when plausible behaviour is never compared with observed outcomes. We introduce GPS-Bench, an evidence-grounded benchmark for governance policy simulation that links policies to relevant actors, actor actions and downstream impacts using legislative records, lobbying disclosures, regulatory documents, corporate filings, economic data and other public evidence. Actors are reconstructed from the dated record rather than prompted as archetypes, so a persona is an evidence object with provenance; a human-annotated pool forms the Gold evaluation set, while cases labelled by a separate LLM from retrieved evidence are treated as Silver supervision and never as test labels. Because every inference mode reads the same grounded state and emits the same schema, GPS-Bench turns "does multi-agent simulation help?" into a controlled comparison: we contrast joint reasoning, independent and communicating actor agents, graph-based methods and weight-level fine-tuning over one policy state. Fine-tuning on the grounded record gives the strongest actor-level impact prediction, and decomposition does not beat it; what decomposition adds is mechanism. Agents hold private, non-identical evidence, each seeing its own exposure clause, and address named partners with concrete joint proposals, what they offer, what they need in return, and why acting together beats acting alone, so the coalitions that form can be checked against the commitments the record holds. GPS-Bench therefore gives a common empirical setting for studying when evidence, actor modelling and multi-agent interaction improve the prediction and interpretation of policy outcomes.
2609.03553.paper_summary_zh: 政策分析不僅僅是預測一項提案是否會通過：它還需要確定誰將受到影響、這些行為者的反應以及隨之而來的結果。基於LLM的政策模擬在大規模上建模這些過程，但當合理的行為從未與觀察到的結果進行比較時，其有效性難以確立。我們介紹GPS-Bench，一個以證據為基礎的治理政策模擬基準，通過立法記錄、遊說披露、監管文件、企業申報、經濟數據和其他公共證據，將政策與相關行為者、行為者行動和下游影響聯繫起來。行為者是從過時的記錄中重建的，而不是作為原型被提示，因此角色是一個具有來源的證據對象；人工標註的池形成了黃金評估集，而由從檢索證據中獲得的獨立LLM標註的案例則被視為銀級監督，而不是測試標籤。因為每個推理模式都讀取相同的基礎狀態並發出相同的模式，GPS-Bench將“多代理模擬有幫助嗎？”轉變為一個受控比較：我們對比了聯合推理、獨立和溝通的行為者代理、基於圖的方法以及在一個政策狀態上的權重級微調。在基礎記錄上進行微調能提供最強的行為者級影響預測，而分解並未超越它；分解所增加的是機制。代理持有私有的、非同質的證據，每個代理看到自己的曝光條款，並以具體的聯合提案來解決命名的合作夥伴，說明他們提供的內容、他們需要什麼作為回報，以及為什麼共同行動優於單獨行動，因此形成的聯盟可以與記錄所持的承諾進行檢查。因此，GPS-Bench提供了一個共同的實證環境，用於研究何時證據、行為者建模和多代理互動改善政策結果的預測和解釋。
